summary: Install-time native addon decodes and executes opaque sibling payload with sandbox/CI/debugger evasion
details: @testsecuiitytestme/cache-helper@1.0.1 is a staged dropper that runs attacker-controlled code at npm install. package.json declares a postinstall hook that requires one of two shipped native addons (addon.node on Linux, addon_win.node on Windows). Both addons reference an adjacent 2.4 MB file `.napi_cache` that contains zero printable strings (fully encrypted or compressed), decode it to a temporary JavaScript file (`/tmp/.%u` on Linux, `%s.nc%lu.js` on Windows), hide/mark it executable (SetFileAttributesA / chmod), and spawn it under node (Linux: fork + setsid + execlp; Windows: CreateProcessA with `node "%s"`). The addons also carry an evasion layer that gates execution on environment inspection: enumeration of CI/sandbox indicator variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, SANDBOX), container checks (/proc/1/cgroup, docker, containerd, kubepod, podman), debugger probes (TracerPid, /proc/self/maps, IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent), and Windows process-name checks for wireshark/procmon/procexp/x64dbg. The package name itself (`testsecuiitytestme`) and the absence of any legitimate caching functionality are consistent with a lure package whose sole purpose is to deliver the opaque payload. The combination of install-time hook, native-addon loader, opaque multi-megabyte sibling blob, and sandbox/CI/debugger evasion is a canonical install-time RCE dropper that evades scanners and executes only on real developer machines.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
